# bugs #3489: sdcpp reports a missing C++ compiler for a C file with a .cpp name although -x c is given

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/3489/
- Category: [Already fixed in trunk](../../fixed-upstream.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17176
- Recommended action: Close as fixed in r13713, which passes -xc to sdcpp.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

The command line of the ticket works on r17176. For a C source file with the name
`sketch.ino.cpp`, `sdcc -c -E -MC -mmcs51 -x c` exits with 0 and writes a dependency rule to the
file that `-o` names. sdcc reads `-MC` as `-M`. `sdcc -E -x c` writes the preprocessed code, and
`sdcc -c -x c` compiles the file. The compile was run for mcs51 with the small, medium, large, and
huge models and with `--stack-auto` for small and large. `sdcc -V` shows `-xc` in the command line
of sdcpp.

sdcpp alone still prints the ticket's message when it is called on the file without `-x c`, and
it succeeds with `-x c`. The reporter shows the same pair of calls in the second comment.

## Fixed by

[r13713](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/13713/), "pass -xc to sdcpp". It adds `-xc` to the
preprocessor command `_preCmd` in `src/SDCCmain.c`. sdcpp then treats every input file as C and
does not select the language by the extension of the file name. In the third comment a maintainer
names r13710 for this change. r13710 changes only a regression test for UTF-8 in identifiers.
